summary.whatChanges: The RPC client now skips header and cookie entries whose value is `undefined` instead of sending them as the literal string "undefined", and omits the Cookie header entirely when no cookie values remain. Tests cover both cases.
behaviorChanges: Headers passed as undefined (from args.header or the client's headers option) are no longer sent with the value "undefined"; they are omitted.
Cookie entries with undefined values are dropped from the serialized Cookie header.
No Cookie header is sent at all when every provided cookie value is undefined (previously an empty Cookie header was sent).
Servers receiving these requests now see missing headers/cookies rather than bogus values, so `c.req.header(...)` returns undefined.
risks: Code depending on the previous behavior (receiving an empty Cookie header or a header literally set to "undefined") will now see the header absent.
Headers are now built by iterating and calling set(), so multi-value header semantics from the previous Headers constructor input could differ.
